extension_contract: tbx.Commafy(n int) string formats an integer with comma thousands separators. Digits are grouped in threes counted from the RIGHT (1000 -> "1,000"; 1234567 -> "1,234,567"). Values with three or fewer digits get no comma (0 -> "0"; 42 -> "42"; 999 -> "999"). Negative values keep a single leading minus in front of the grouped magnitude (-1500 -> "-1,500"; -42 -> "-42"; -1234567 -> "-1,234,567"). The helper is two functions: tbxCommafy(n) dispatches the sign and delegates digit grouping to tbxGroup(s string).
injection_strategy: Two coupled single-region defects in one new file stdlib/core/tbx.go, both symptoms surfaced in the prompt with examples. Fixing the obvious grouping bug alone leaves the negative-sign bug failing.

bugs.defect: Comma boundary is computed from the LEFT edge (`i % 3 == 0`) instead of from the right (`(len(s) - i) % 3 == 0`), so commas are inserted counting from the start of the digit string rather than the end.
bugs.symptom: Grouping is misplaced for any value whose digit count is not a multiple of three: 1234 -> "123,4", 1000 -> "100,0", 1234567 -> "123,456,7". Two- and three-digit values happen to be unaffected. This is the obvious symptom; the prompt gives 1234 and 1234567 as examples.

bugs.defect: For n < 0 the function returns tbxGroup(strconv.Itoa(-n)) — it negates n to get the magnitude but never re-attaches the leading minus, so the sign is silently dropped. The fix prepends "-" to the grouped magnitude.
bugs.symptom: Negative numbers lose their sign: -42 -> "42", -1500 -> "150,0" (also shows BUG_A grouping), -1234567 -> "123,456,7". A careless fix that only corrects tbxGroup's boundary still drops the sign: -1500 would become "1,500", -42 would become "42".

expected_failure_summary: Accepted (correct tbx.go) 12/12 = 1.000. Broken fails 6/12 (3 BUG_A grouping + 3 BUG_B negatives), passes 6 short non-negative controls -> 6/12 = 0.500, well below the 0.9 gate and inside the 0.4-0.6 medium band.
partial_fix_traps: Fixing only the grouping boundary in tbxGroup (BUG_A) — the most obvious symptom — leaves the three negative checks failing because the sign is still dropped: 9/12 = 0.750, still below the gate.
Fixing only the sign handling (BUG_B) leaves the three positive grouping checks failing: 9/12 = 0.750.
Both the right-edge grouping and the leading-minus must be restored for a full pass; the two defects sit in two different functions in the same file.
note: The bespoke tbx extension auto-registers because the harness blank-imports stdlib/core, whose init() populates stdlib.Values["tbx"]. No other wiring is touched. The registration boilerplate in init() is outside both bug regions.
